svg.title: One shared map, three kinds of traffic
svg.desc: Three clients (a desktop browser drawing, a keyboard-first browser drawing, a phone drawing while a crew watches) exchange three kinds of traffic with the Snapland server: live drafts, saved areas and presence. Only saved areas reach the database.
svg.text: One shared map, three kinds of traffic
Noa, desktop browser
mouse, aerial imagery, is drawing
wants a km² figure she can trust
and a history she can roll back
Rina, keyboard-first browser
no mouse, screen reader some days
draws, names and saves by keys only
needs a text alternative to the map
Avi, phone in a vehicle
patchy 4G, one hand, is drawing
work zones while his crews watch
keeps working when the socket drops
Snapland
nginx edge + two backend replicas
PostgreSQL + PostGIS
areas, versions, users, sessions, audit
computes km² on the WGS84 ellipsoid
Redis
drafts, presence, locks, rate limits
pub/sub between the two replicas
WebSocket gateway
subprotocol snapland.v1, one socket
per browser tab, filtered by viewport
Live draft, every point as it is placed
ephemeral, at most 10 updates/s, never stored
Saved area, name + polygon -> authoritative km²
durable, versioned, written once over REST, then broadcast
Presence, who is viewing or drawing right now
ephemeral, refreshed every 15 s, expires when a tab closes
Caption: every browser talks to the same server, but only the saved area reaches the database. Drafts and presence
are relayed through Redis and forgotten. Chapter 2 draws the full system model; this picture only names the three flows.
